body.working_title: Bias of the occurrence probability in iETS inverse-odds and odds-ratio models

body.text: Are the occurrence probability and point forecasts of the iETS inverse-odds-ratio (iETS_I) and odds-ratio (iETS_O) models biased when estimated with the error proxies of Svetunkov and Boylan (2023), and how does any bias compare with that of Croston's method?

body.definition: Inverse odds ratio occurrence model (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, eq. 18): o_t ~ Bernoulli(p_t), p_t = 1/(1+mu_b,t), mu_b,t = l_b,t-1, l_b,t = l_b,t-1 (1 + alpha_b e_b,t); in smooth: occurrence='inverse-odds-ratio' (C++ case 'i' in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h).
Odds ratio occurrence model (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, eq. 16): p_t = mu_a,t/(mu_a,t+1), mu_a,t = l_a,t-1, l_a,t = l_a,t-1 (1 + alpha_a e_a,t); in smooth: occurrence='odds-ratio' (C++ case 'o').

Proxy for the unobservable occurrence error (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, eqs. 24-25): u_t = (1 + o_t - p_hat_t)/2; iETS_O: 1 + e_a,t = u_t/(1-u_t); iETS_I: 1 + e_b,t = (1-u_t)/u_t. With an additive-error occurrence state (smooth's EA='A') the state is updated with log(1 + e) instead.
The recursion that produces p_hat_t from the observed o_t, the initial level and the smoothing parameter, with the state updated through the error proxy on every observation.
Croston (1972): SES on demand intervals q and sizes z, updated only at demand occurrences; probability forecast 1/q_hat.
Long-run mean of p_hat_t produced by an occurrence filter applied to o_t ~ Bernoulli(p) with constant p, after a burn-in; compared with the true p.
Simulated o_t, independent Bernoulli(p) draws with p fixed over time.

body.text: Before this record was started, the agent ran an unrecorded scratchpad simulation of the iETS_I and iETS_O occurrence filters (constant p, alpha in {0.01,0.05,0.1,0.3}) and derived fixed points 1-sqrt(1-p) and sqrt(p) analytically; it reported them to the human in chat. That simulation is rerun as the first recorded exploratory run, and every hypothesis it informed is recorded as from exploration.

body.design: Simulate o_t ~ Bernoulli(p), p in {0.02, 0.15, 0.4, 0.65, 0.9} (none used in RN1), alpha = 0.002 (not used in RN1), T = 4,000,000 per cell, burn-in 200,000, seeds 1001 onwards (new). Run smooth's occurrenceError() (src/headers/ssOccurrence.h) as the state update for iETS_I and iETS_O with multiplicative and with additive occurrence error, and Croston's 1/q_hat; every filter starts at the true value. Script: claimset/code/iets-occurrence-bias/stationary_probability.py with grid_confirm.json.
body.analysis: Per cell, the mean of p_hat after burn-in. Per (model, error), the largest relative deviation |mean - predicted| / predicted over the five p values, where predicted is 1 - sqrt(1 - p) (iETS_I, M), sqrt(p) (iETS_O, M), the root of p log(x/(2-x)) + (1-p) log((1+x)/(1-x)) = 0 (both models, A) and p (Croston). Any non-finite state counts as a deviation of at least 1.

body.rationale: Rule of PL2 met: largest relative deviation from 1 - sqrt(1 - p) over five new p values is 0.0041 < tolerance 0.02.
Rule of PL3 met: largest relative deviation from sqrt(p) is 0.0036 < tolerance 0.02.
Rule of PL4 met: largest relative deviations from the predicted root are 0.0014 (iETS_I) and 0.0032 (iETS_O), both < 0.02.
Rule of PL5 met: largest relative deviation of Croston's 1/q_hat from p at alpha = 0.002 is 0.0049 < 0.02.

body.definition: Inverse odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 18): o_t ~ Bernoulli(p_t), p_t = 1/(1+mu_b,t), mu_b,t = l_b,t-1, l_b,t = l_b,t-1 (1 + alpha_b e_b,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_b,t = log l_b,t-1 + alpha_b e_b,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='inverse-odds-ratio' (C++ case 'i' in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h).
body.source: Svetunkov, I. and Boylan, J.E. (2023). iETS: State space model for intermittent demand forecasting. International Journal of Production Economics 265, 109013. doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2023.109013

body.definition: Odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 16): p_t = mu_a,t/(mu_a,t+1), mu_a,t = l_a,t-1, l_a,t = l_a,t-1 (1 + alpha_a e_a,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_a,t = log l_a,t-1 + alpha_a e_a,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='odds-ratio' (C++ case 'o').
body.source: Svetunkov, I. and Boylan, J.E. (2023). iETS: State space model for intermittent demand forecasting. International Journal of Production Economics 265, 109013. doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2023.109013

body.definition: The proxy for the unobservable occurrence error that smooth uses (occurrenceError() in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h): v_t = o_t - p_hat_t, u_t = (1 + v_t)/2; iETS_O: 1 + e_a,t = u_t/(1-u_t) = (1+v_t)/(1-v_t); iETS_I: 1 + e_b,t = (1-u_t)/u_t. With an additive occurrence error the log of the same ratio is used.
body.source: Svetunkov, I. and Boylan, J.E. (2023). iETS: State space model for intermittent demand forecasting. International Journal of Production Economics 265, 109013. doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2023.109013 (eqs. 24-25, Appendix A)

body.definition: Croston (1972): SES on demand intervals q and sizes z, updated only at demand occurrences; probability forecast 1/q_hat.
body.source: Croston, J.D. (1972). Forecasting and stock control for intermittent demands. Operational Research Quarterly 23(3), 289-303.

body.definition: Proxy proposed in this study: the score of the Bernoulli occurrence log-likelihood o log p + (1-o) log(1-p) with respect to the log of the state, at p_hat_t: e_a,t = o_t - p_hat_t (mu_a: iETS_O, iETS_G) and e_b,t = p_hat_t - o_t (mu_b: iETS_I, iETS_G). Additive error: log mu_t = log mu_t-1 + alpha e_t (a score-driven filter with unit scaling); multiplicative error: mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + alpha e_t). Derivation: derivations.md section 4.
body.source: Creal, D., Koopman, S.J. and Lucas, A. (2013). Generalized autoregressive score models with applications. Journal of Applied Econometrics 28(5), 777-795. doi:10.1002/jae.1279; Harvey, A.C. (2013). Dynamic Models for Volatility and Heavy Tails. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9781139540933

body.definition: For an occurrence filter applied to o_t ~ Bernoulli(p), the value x of p_hat at which the expected update of the state, E[e_t | p_hat_t = x], is zero (derivations.md section 1).

Observation-driven time series models whose time-varying parameter is updated by a scaled score of the conditional log-likelihood (generalised autoregressive score / dynamic conditional score models).
body.source: Creal, Koopman and Lucas (2013), doi:10.1002/jae.1279; Harvey (2013), doi:10.1017/CBO9781139540933

body.definition: Recursions theta_t = theta_t-1 + alpha H(theta_t-1, o_t) with fixed gain alpha; as alpha tends to 0 their iterates concentrate around the stable zeros of the mean dynamics d theta/dt = E[H(theta, o)] (the ODE method).
body.source: Benveniste, A., Metivier, M. and Priouret, P. (1990). Adaptive Algorithms and Stochastic Approximations. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-642-75894-2; Kushner, H.J. and Yin, G.G. (2003). Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed. Springer. doi:10.1007/b97441

body.definition: The upward bias of Croston's 1/q_hat as an estimate of the occurrence probability, from Jensen's inequality applied to an SES of the demand intervals; of order alpha.
body.source: Syntetos, A.A. and Boylan, J.E. (2001). On the bias of intermittent demand estimates. International Journal of Production Economics 71(1-3), 457-466. doi:10.1016/S0925-5273(00)00143-2; Syntetos, A.A. and Boylan, J.E. (2005). The accuracy of intermittent demand estimates. International Journal of Forecasting 21(2), 303-314. doi:10.1016/j.ijforecast.2004.10.001

body.definition: Stationary mean probability minus the true p, for an occurrence filter applied to Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability p; estimated by simulation with a batch-means Monte Carlo standard error.

body.term: alpha-to-0 limit of the stationary mean probability
body.definition: For a filter and a p, the intercept at alpha = 0 of the least-squares line of the stationary mean probability on alpha, fitted to simulations at small alpha values; compared with the zero-drift point.

body.term: random design over p and alpha
body.definition: Pairs (p, alpha) drawn at random with a fixed seed: p uniform on [0.02, 0.98] and log(alpha) uniform on [log 0.001, log 1]; or values of p drawn uniformly on [0.02, 0.98], each simulated at a fixed set of small alpha values. Each cell: one simulated series of Bernoulli occurrences, filter started at the true value, burn-in discarded, batch means for the standard error.

body.text: Study code lives in claimset/code/iets-occurrence-bias/ on the code branch iets-occurrence-bias, not claimset-code/: smooth keeps all claimset material in one root folder, claimset/, already left out of package builds by '^claimset$' in .Rbuildignore. Chosen with the human (AC1).

body.description: Derivations of the drift of the old and score occurrence proxies, their zero-drift points and the score property, with references; one section per formal hypothesis (H5 section 2, H6 section 3, H7 section 4). Checked by derivations_check.py.

body.statement: For a fixed p and an occurrence filter with a unique stable zero-drift point x*, the stationary mean of p_hat converges to x* as alpha tends to 0 (constant-gain stochastic approximation, ODE method). The regularity conditions of the theorems are not verified for these filters; H8, H10 and H12 test the consequence by simulation.

body.text: H5-H12 restate the study's hypotheses for every p in (0,1) and every alpha in (0,1], at the request of the human (AC1): H1-H3 (decided at alpha = 0.002) are special cases of H6 and H8, and H4 of H12. H1-H4 and their verdicts stay in the record.

body.statement: For every p in (0,1), the [[TM10:old error proxy]] has a non-zero expected value at the true probability: with o ~ Bernoulli(p) and p_hat = p, E[1 + e_a] = 2 - p + (1-p)^2/(1+p) > 1 and E[1 + e_b] = 1 + p + p^2/(2-p) > 1 (multiplicative error), and E[log(1 + e_a)] = -E[log(1 + e_b)] is positive for p < 0.5, zero at 0.5 and negative above (additive error); the cause is the convexity of the proxy in the unbiased residual o - p_hat.
body.question: Q1

about.subject: TM10
about.relation: has non-zero expected value at the true probability

body.statement: For every p in (0,1), the [[TM4:occurrence filters]] with the [[TM10:old error proxy]] have a unique stable [[TM13:zero-drift point]]: 1 - sqrt(1-p) < p for [[TM1:iETS_I]] and sqrt(p) > p for [[TM2:iETS_O]] with multiplicative error, and, for both models with additive error, the root of p log(x/(2-x)) + (1-p) log((1+x)/(1-x)) = 0, which lies between p and 0.5.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: The [[TM12:score proxy]] is the score of the Bernoulli occurrence log-likelihood with respect to the log of the state for [[TM1:iETS_I]] (p_hat - o) and [[TM2:iETS_O]] (o - p_hat); for every p in (0,1) its [[TM13:zero-drift point]] is p itself, unique and stable, and with multiplicative error it keeps the state positive for every alpha in (0,1].
body.question: Q1

body.statement: On [[TM7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]] p, for every p in (0,1), as alpha tends to 0, the stationary mean probability of [[TM1:iETS_I]] and [[TM2:iETS_O]] with the [[TM10:old error proxy]], under either occurrence error type, converges to the [[TM13:zero-drift point]] of H6, not to p: the bias of the old filters does not vanish with a small smoothing parameter.
body.question: Q1

about.subject: old error proxy filters
about.relation: have alpha-to-0 limit of the stationary mean equal to

body.statement: On [[TM7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]] p, for every p in (0,1) and every alpha in (0,1], the [[TM17:bias of the occurrence probability]] of the [[TM10:old error proxy]] filters has a fixed direction: negative for [[TM1:iETS_I]] and positive for [[TM2:iETS_O]] with multiplicative error, and towards 0.5 (the stationary mean lies between p and 0.5) for both models with additive error.
body.question: Q1

body.statement: On [[TM7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]] p, for every p in (0,1), as alpha tends to 0, the stationary mean probability of [[TM1:iETS_I]] and [[TM2:iETS_O]] with the [[TM12:score proxy]], under either occurrence error type, converges to p: the bias of the score filters vanishes with the smoothing parameter.
body.question: Q1

about.subject: TM12
about.relation: has alpha-to-0 limit of the stationary mean equal to

body.statement: On [[TM7:Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability]] p, for every p in (0,1) and every alpha in (0,1], the absolute [[TM17:bias of the occurrence probability]] of [[TM1:iETS_I]] and [[TM2:iETS_O]] is smaller with the [[TM12:score proxy]] than with the [[TM10:old error proxy]], under either occurrence error type.

body.design: 30 values of p drawn uniformly on [0.02, 0.98] (design seed in the file); each simulated at alpha in {0.004, 0.002, 0.001}; T = 20,000,000 per cell, burn-in 2,000,000, 100 batches for the standard error; filter started at the true value. iETS_I and iETS_O, multiplicative and additive occurrence error, old proxy (smooth's occurrenceError()). Script: general_design.py design_limit_old.json.
body.analysis: Per filter and p, the intercept at alpha = 0 of the least-squares line of the stationary mean on alpha; relative deviation |intercept - prediction| / prediction; per filter, the largest over the 30 values of p. A non-finite state in any cell counts as a deviation of 1. Prediction: the zero-drift point of H6.
body.new_data: A new random design (its own seed): no value of p or alpha, and no seed, of RN1-RN5.

body.design: 200 pairs (p, alpha), p uniform on [0.02, 0.98], log(alpha) uniform on [log 0.001, log 1] (design seed in the file); T = 20,000,000 per cell, burn-in 2,000,000, 100 batches; filter started at the true value. iETS_I and iETS_O, multiplicative and additive occurrence error, old proxy. Script: general_design.py design_direction_old.json.
body.analysis: Per cell, bias = stationary mean - p with its standard error. A cell has the wrong direction if the bias is on the wrong side by more than z = 4 standard errors: above p for iETS_I (M), below p for iETS_O (M), and for the additive error beyond p away from 0.5 or beyond 0.5; or if a state became non-finite. Count per filter.
